_what: The Trillion apps a person can put on their devices, one row per kind, read by src/devices.mjs for every place they are offered: the devices section of Use Trillion in your AI (which the welcome tour's devices step points at), start_setup's install.devices, and the setup prompt's {devices_step}. A row says what it is (title, body, and domain: the web address whose logo leads its row), how Trillion knows this account already has it (installed_when.signs_in_as: the names the app signs in under; a sign-in on the account under one of these names means it is installed), what each app brings that a web page cannot (brings: ids such as listen; a screen that needs one offers, right there, the apps that bring it and that this account does not have yet, through /work/api/screens/get-the-app?for=<id>, headed by words.brings.<id>), on which systems its link is also drawn as a code to scan with a phone (scan_on: a computer, for an app that goes on a phone; /devices/scan draws only links listed here), what it offers once installed (once_installed: a tour, such as how to share to Trillion from it, by its id in src/workspace/walkthroughs, or `queue`: a job in src/queued-work.json the person's own AI is handed, such as putting free AI models on the Mac), and where to get it per system (get: one entry per set of systems, `systems` either "any" or system ids; `href` is the public install address, or null with `not_yet` saying honestly why it cannot be installed yet). `systems` tells a device's system from its User-Agent, first match wins (an iPhone's User-Agent also says Mac OS X, and an Android one says Linux, so they come first). `words` are the section's and the setup prompt's own words. A new device kind, a new system or a newly published link is one change here; nothing that draws or composes changes. Distribution-backed routes require a fresh operator-owned observation. Their configured href is only a Check access recovery address until current distribution and observer eligibility are known; it never proves installation. Provider constraints are public, and a personal preference cannot create provider evidence.
